title: Build a Strong Portfolio with AI

blocks.text: The Portfolio Shouldn't Take Weeks to Build

You know your work is strong. You've delivered results, solved problems, and built things that matter. But when someone asks to see your portfolio, you freeze.

Where do you even start? What should you include? How do you make it look professional without being a designer?

Luckily, AI nowadays can help you with the hardest part — planning and structure. This guide will show you how it's done!
The Blank Page Problem
Most professionals never build a portfolio. Not because they lack achievements, but because the process feels overwhelming.

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly! Structure is the real blocker — not your achievements or available time. Once you know what to build and how to organize it, the actual building becomes manageable.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Time feels like the issue, but it's actually a symptom. Without a clear structure, even hours of work lead nowhere. Structure first, then building becomes quick.

options.label: Not having enough good work to showcase
Finding time to actually sit down and build it
Not knowing how to organize or structure it

blocks.question: Think of yourself. If you think about building a portfolio, what stops you most?

blocks.text:
This is how it usually happens: you open a blank document or website builder and think: "What sections do I need? How should I organize this? Should I start with my bio or my work?"

Then, nothing gets done. Meanwhile, others with portfolios — sometimes with less impressive work — keep landing opportunities.

In such situations, AI can truly help. However, it isn't here to write your portfolio for you or invent achievements you don't have. It's here to handle the hardest early step: giving you a clear, logical structure so you can stop staring at a blank page and start building.
AI as Your Planning Partner

Think of AI as the friend who asks the right questions and helps you organize your thoughts.

You already know your work. AI just helps you structure it in a way that makes sense to others.

feedbackCorrect.text: AI excels at giving you frameworks and structure — you bring your actual work, goals, and professional judgment.

feedbackIncorrect.text: AI handles the "how to organize this" questions brilliantly, but decisions about your career direction require your own expertise and goals.

options.label: Deciding which career path you should pursue next
Suggesting what sections a portfolio should include
Creating an outline so you know where to start
Organizing your projects into logical categories

blocks.text: Starting With ChatGPT
Let's see how this works in practice with ChatGPT — one of the simplest AI tools for planning.

ChatGPT can help you create a clear portfolio structure in seconds. You ask a simple question, and it gives you a logical framework to work from.

No more guessing what sections you need. No more second-guessing yourself for hours.

feedbackCorrect.text: Perfect! A clear, specific question gets you a useful framework you can customize to your situation.

feedbackIncorrect.text: AI works best when you ask for structure and guidance — not for it to do everything or make personal decisions for you.

blocks.question: If you're building a professional portfolio, what do you think is the best question to ask ChatGPT?

blocks.text: Let's try it. Imagine you want a simple, professional portfolio structure.

blocks.exampleResponse:
Here's a clean, effective structure for a professional portfolio:
  1. About — Who you are and what you do
  2. Work/Projects — Your best achievements with brief descriptions
  3. Skills — Key competencies and expertise areas
  4. Experience — Career timeline or notable roles
  5. Contact — How people can reach you

options.label: It includes every possible thing someone might want to know about you

blocks.question: Looking at this structure, what's its biggest advantage?

blocks.text: Making It Yours
This is a starting point — not a rigid template. You can adjust it based on your field and goals.
Now you have a clear outline. You know what sections you need. The blank page problem? Solved.

So, maybe you're in a creative field and want to lead with visuals. Or you're a consultant who needs case studies instead of a simple project list. Or you're working anywhere else — that's all fine! 

The point is you now have a framework to customize, not a blank page to stare at.
Beyond Structure
ChatGPT helped you with the first step — organization. But portfolio building doesn't stop there.
In the upcoming lessons, you'll learn how to:

• Define your visual identity with AI-generated moodboards
  • Write clear project descriptions without spending hours editing
  • Design layouts without needing professional design skills
  • Publish your portfolio as a real website — no coding required
All using AI tools that handle the technical work while you focus on showcasing your strengths.
You've Taken the First Step!

You've just learned how AI removes the hardest part of portfolio building — figuring out where to start.

No more blank pages. No more analysis paralysis. Just a clear structure you can start filling in immediately.

In the next lesson, you'll define your visual identity — the colors, style, and overall feel that make your portfolio uniquely yours. AI will help you discover your aesthetic without needing design experience. Let's keep building!

blocks.title: Key Takeaways

blocks.text: Your Portfolio Needs a Look

What separates amateur portfolios from professional ones? Visual consistency. Colors that work together. A clear style. An intentional atmosphere that makes people think, "This person knows what they're doing." The good news: you don't need design school to create this. AI can help you discover your visual identity in minutes!
What Is a Visual Identity?
Think of the visual identity as your portfolio's personality. It's the first impression people get before they even read your work.
Hence, your visual identity is the combination of colors, style, and atmosphere that makes your portfolio feel like yours.

feedbackCorrect.text: That's right! Consistency signals thoughtfulness and professionalism — not technical skill. Even simple portfolios look polished when the visual language is cohesive.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Consistency isn't about showing off design expertise — it's about creating a unified experience that feels intentional and trustworthy.

options.label: It shows you have advanced design skills
It makes your portfolio longer and more impressive
It makes you look professional and intentional, even if your work is simple

blocks.question: Before diving in, why do you think visual consistency matters in a portfolio?

blocks.text: The Visual Chaos Problem
Most people building portfolios make the same mistake: they start adding content without deciding how it should look first.

One project uses bright colors. Another uses muted tones. Fonts don't match. The overall feeling is... scattered. It's not that individual pieces look bad — it's that nothing feels intentional. Professional portfolios have a cohesive visual language that ties everything together.

feedbackCorrect.text: When color palette, visual style, and tone align, your portfolio feels cohesive and intentional.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Visual identity relies on consistency, not variety. A focused combination of colors, style, and tone creates a unified look, while mixing too many elements makes things feel random.

options.label: A color palette with 3-5 colors that work well together
A defined tone or atmosphere, such as professional, friendly, or creative
Many various fonts and design elements
A clear visual style like minimalist, bold, or organic

blocks.question: What elements do you think make up a good visual identity?

feedbackCorrect.text: Right! Your visual identity should match your audience's expectations. Corporate clients trust clean, professional aesthetics.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Visual identity is about what makes your target audience feel confident working with you. Corporate clients trust clean, professional aesthetics!

options.label: Clean, professional, with neutral colors and simple layouts
Bright, playful, with bold colors and hand-drawn elements
Dark, edgy, with high contrast and unconventional fonts

blocks.question: Next, if you're a consultant who works with corporate clients, which visual identity makes the most sense?

blocks.text:
The corporate world is only one example, and it requires certain visual language. But what about other cases? Portfolios can be styled in various ways: modern and minimal, warm and approachable, bold and creative. 

Which style to choose? AI will help you define this clearly!
Meet Midjourney
Midjourney is an AI tool that generates images from text descriptions. But it's not just for creating artwork — it's perfect for exploring visual ideas before you commit to anything.

You can ask Midjourney to generate moodboards, color palettes, and style references. It shows you what different visual identities look like, helping you figure out what resonates with you.

No design experience required. You just describe what you want, and Midjourney visualizes it.
For example, say you want a portfolio that feels modern but approachable. Not too corporate, not too casual.

blocks.text:
See what happened? You described the feeling you wanted, and Midjourney turned it into a visual reference.

Now you're not guessing what "modern but friendly" means — you can see it, refine it, and use it as your guide.

feedbackCorrect.text: Right! Just like you did it above, exploring visually saves time and prevents costly mistakes. You'll know what works before you start building.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Skipping this step means guessing your way through design decisions later. A clear visual direction upfront makes every choice easier.

blocks.text: Trying Different Styles
You're not locked into your first attempt. Midjourney lets you experiment with different aesthetics quickly.

Want to see what a bold, high-contrast version looks like? Or a softer, pastel approach? Generate a few options and compare them side by side.

This is how you discover your natural aesthetic — by seeing what resonates emotionally when you look at it.

blocks.prompt: Generate a different moodboard to compare aesthetics.
blocks.template: [Style], [tone], [color description] brand moodboard

feedbackCorrect.text: Smart! Choosing one clear direction and committing to it creates consistency. Mixing too many styles creates visual chaos.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Consistency comes from commitment. Pick the aesthetic that serves your goals best, then use it throughout your portfolio.

options.label: Keep generating more options until you find something perfect
Combine elements from all of them into one design
Pick the one that best matches your goals and audience, then go with it

blocks.question: So, you generated more than one moodboard. What should you do next?

blocks.text: Building Your Identity Sheet in Canva
Once you choose your visual direction, it's time to turn it into a reference document you can use while building your portfolio.

Canva lets you combine your chosen colors, style examples, and atmosphere into one clean visual identity sheet. This becomes your guide — every time you make a design decision, you check: Does this match my identity sheet?
To elaborate on what you already learned, your identity sheet should include:

• 3-5 core colors (pulled from your chosen moodboard)
  • Style descriptors (minimalist, warm, approachable)
  • Visual examples (screenshots from your Midjourney moodboard)
  • Font suggestions (optional — Canva can recommend these)

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly! Your identity sheet is your consistency guide. Weeks from now, you'll still make design choices that feel cohesive.

feedbackIncorrect.text: The identity sheet isn't for showing off — it's a practical tool that keeps your portfolio visually unified as you build it piece by piece.

options.label: It proves to others that you have design skills
It's required for publishing your portfolio online
It ensures consistency across all portfolio sections, even as you build over time

blocks.question: But why create a visual identity sheet instead of just remembering what you liked?

blocks.text: Okay, you know why you need it and what to include there, but how to create this sheet? Well, instead of building everything manually, Canva can generate the layout for you:

1. Create a new document.
  2. Upload your chosen Midjourney moodboard in the space for prompts.
  3. Put this prompt: "Create a visual identity sheet using these images. Include a color palette, style keywords, and font suggestions in a clean layout."
As a result, Canva will instantly build a structured identity sheet you can refine in seconds.

Just like that, you will have a mock-up visual identity guideline in a few minutes! Then, you can manually edit the document if you want to improve the result.

When you're done, save it somewhere accessible — you'll reference it constantly as you build your portfolio sections.
You've Defined Your Visual DNA!

You just learned how to use AI to discover and document your portfolio's visual identity — something that used to require hiring a brand designer.

Now you have a clear aesthetic direction. Every design choice from here forward will align with this foundation.
In the next lesson, you'll learn how to choose and curate your best work — picking 3-5 strong projects and writing clear, compelling descriptions using AI. Let's keep building!

AI can help you discover your visual identity in minutes!
What Is a Visual Identity?
Think of the visual identity as your portfolio's personality. It's the first impression people get before they even read your work.
Hence, your visual identity is the combination of colors, style, and atmosphere that makes your portfolio feel like yours.

blocks.text: The "Too Much" Problem

You've defined your structure. You've nailed your visual identity. Now comes the hardest question: what work should you actually show? Often, people panic here. They want to include everything — every project, every achievement, every skill they've ever demonstrated. Let's see how to make your portfolio really effective!
Why Showing Everything Backfires
When you include every project you've ever done, something strange happens: people stop paying attention. But why is it so?

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly! When everything in your portfolio is strong, people assume all your work meets that standard. Diluting it with weaker projects lowers their overall impression.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Curation isn't about speed or appearing less intimidating — it's about quality control. Showing only your strongest work makes your expertise undeniable.

options.label: It makes you look more approachable because many projects might imply that you're too good
It's faster to build, so you can publish and use your portfolio sooner
It forces you to show only your best work, making quality obvious

blocks.question: Fewer projects can make a stronger impression than many projects. Why?

blocks.text:
Think about it yourself. What would you do if you saw 20 projects in the portfolio? Probably, you would say, "I'll look at this later" — then never do. Or, you would skim and remember nothing specific.

Meanwhile, portfolios with 3-5 carefully chosen projects get studied closely. People actually read the descriptions and understand what you're good at.
Therefore, you should think of your portfolio like a greatest hits compilation. Musicians don't put every song they've ever recorded on it — they choose the tracks that best represent their sound.
Choosing What to Include

So how do you decide which projects make the cut?

The answer lies in the fact that your portfolio should attract the opportunities you actually want, not just display everything you're capable of.

feedbackCorrect.text: Smart! Your portfolio is a tool for attracting future work. Show the kind of projects you want more of, not just what you're proud of.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Showcasing everything sends mixed signals. Clients hire specialists — your portfolio should make it crystal clear what you're great at and want to do.

options.label: Your absolute best projects, even if they don't really match with your goals, to show your versatility
Projects that match the work you want to attract, even if you have stronger work elsewhere

blocks.question: Consider a situation: you've done great work in multiple areas, but you want to focus on one type of client going forward. What should your portfolio emphasize?

blocks.text:
All in all, a simple guideline for most professionals is: choose 3-5 strong projects. Why?
  • Fewer than 3 feels thin — people want proof you've done this more than once
  • More than 5 starts to overwhelm — people won't look at everything carefully
So, three to five projects is the sweet spot where people actually engage with your work instead of skimming past it.

feedbackCorrect.text: These factors ensure your portfolio is strategic, not just a random collection. You're showing work that matters to the people you want to work with.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Time spent doesn't equal value to your audience. Focus on impact, relevance, and clarity — those are what make projects portfolio-worthy.

options.label: Projects that align with the type of work you want to attract

Projects that took you the longest time to complete

blocks.text: Writing Project Descriptions
Once you choose projects, you need to describe them clearly — and this is where most people struggle.
You sit down to write and think: "How do I explain this project in a way that makes sense to someone who wasn't there?" This is where Claude helps.
Meet Claude

With Claude, you won't get stuck in the process when you draft paragraphs, delete them, start over, and after an hour still stare at a half-finished description that feels either too detailed or too vague.

feedbackCorrect.text: Right! Claude is a summarization tool — you provide the facts and context, and Claude shapes them into readable descriptions.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Claude doesn't invent or fabricate. It clarifies and condenses what you tell it, making your real work easier for others to understand quickly.

options.label: It invents impressive-sounding accomplishments to make your work look better
It writes descriptions without needing any input from you
It takes your detailed explanation and summarizes it into clear, concise language

blocks.question: How do you think Claude can help with writing project descriptions?

blocks.text: The process looks like this:

1. You give Claude the details about your project — what you did, what the challenge was, what the outcome was.
  2. Claude turns it into a clean, audience-friendly description.
No more agonizing over every sentence. No more wondering if you sound too technical or too simplistic.
Creating Your First Description
Let's say you want to describe a marketing campaign you led. You have all the details in your head, but turning them into 2-3 clear sentences feels difficult.

blocks.exampleResponse: Here's a concise portfolio description: "Led a digital marketing campaign for a regional retail client facing declining foot traffic. Developed a targeted social media strategy and local partnership program, resulting in a 35% increase in store visits over three months." Clean, clear, and focused on impact.
blocks.prompt: Give Claude the key details about your project and ask it to create a portfolio-ready description.
blocks.template: I led [project type] for [client/context]. The challenge was [problem]. I developed [plan] and a local partnership program, leading to [outcome]. Summarize this into [length] for a professional portfolio.

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly! Good portfolio descriptions follow a simple pattern: problem → solution → result. Readers understand your value quickly.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Effective descriptions are concise and outcome-focused, not exhaustive and not too detailed. You want readers to grasp your impact immediately, not get lost in process details.

options.label: It explains the challenge, your approach, and the measurable outcome in just a few sentences
It uses technical marketing terminology to prove expertise, as well as lists tasks you performed in detail

blocks.question: Looking at this description, what makes it effective for a portfolio?

blocks.text:
See how that works? You provided the raw information, and Claude structured it into a clean narrative.

Now you can do this for each of your 3-5 chosen projects without spending hours rewriting and second-guessing yourself!
Describing Different Project Types
Not every project has clear metrics like "35% increase." Some work is more qualitative — and that's fine.

blocks.exampleResponse: Here's the portfolio description: "Redesigned the internal onboarding process for a 50-person consulting firm. Created streamlined documentation and training materials that reduced new hire ramp-up time and improved team consistency." No specific numbers, but the value is still clear.
blocks.prompt: Ask Claude to summarize a project where the value is qualitative rather than numerical.
blocks.template: I [what you did] the internal onboarding process for [client/context]. The goal was to  [objective]. I created [your approach], which [qualitative outcome] and improved team consistency. Summarize this into [length] for a professional portfolio.

blocks.text: Even without hard metrics, this description clearly communicates value. Claude helped you frame qualitative impact in a concrete, professional way.
Organizing Your Portfolio Assets
You've chosen your projects. You've written clear descriptions. Now you need to organize everything so it's ready for layout. You can do it in Notion.
In Notion, create a simple database or page structure:

• One page per project
  • Include your Claude-written description at the top
  • Add links to visuals, screenshots, or files you'll use in the portfolio
  • Tag each project with relevant categories (client type, skills used, etc.)
This keeps everything accessible and organized when you start designing your actual portfolio pages in the upcoming lessons.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Clients never see your folder structure — this organization is purely practical. It prevents workflow interruptions when you're focused on design and layout.

blocks.text: The "Too Much" Problem

You've defined your structure. You've nailed your visual identity. Now comes the hardest question: what work should you actually show? Often, people panic here. They want to include everything — every project, every achievement, every skill they've ever demonstrated. Let's see how to make your portfolio really effective!
Why Showing Everything Backfires
When you include every project you've ever done, something strange happens: people stop paying attention. But why is it so?

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly! When everything in your portfolio is strong, people assume all your work meets that standard. Diluting it with weaker projects lowers their overall impression.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Curation isn't about speed or appearing less intimidating — it's about quality control. Showing only your strongest work makes your expertise undeniable.

options.label: It makes you look more approachable because many projects might imply that you're too good
It's faster to build, so you can publish and use your portfolio sooner
It forces you to show only your best work, making quality obvious

blocks.question: Fewer projects can make a stronger impression than many projects. Why?

blocks.text:
Think about it yourself. What would you do if you saw 20 projects in the portfolio? Probably, you would say, "I'll look at this later" — then never do. Or, you would skim and remember nothing specific.

Meanwhile, portfolios with 3-5 carefully chosen projects get studied closely. People actually read the descriptions and understand what you're good at.
Therefore, you should think of your portfolio like a greatest hits compilation. Musicians don't put every song they've ever recorded on it — they choose the tracks that best represent their sound.
Choosing What to Include

So how do you decide which projects make the cut?

The answer lies in the fact that your portfolio should attract the opportunities you actually want, not just display everything you're capable of.

feedbackCorrect.text: Smart! Your portfolio is a tool for attracting future work. Show the kind of projects you want more of, not just what you're proud of.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Showcasing everything sends mixed signals. Clients hire specialists — your portfolio should make it crystal clear what you're great at and want to do.

options.label: Your absolute best projects, even if they don't really match with your goals, to show your versatility
Projects that match the work you want to attract, even if you have stronger work elsewhere

blocks.question: Consider a situation: you've done great work in multiple areas, but you want to focus on one type of client going forward. What should your portfolio emphasize?

blocks.text:
All in all, a simple guideline for most professionals is: choose 3-5 strong projects. Why?
  • Fewer than 3 feels thin — people want proof you've done this more than once
  • More than 5 starts to overwhelm — people won't look at everything carefully
So, three to five projects is the sweet spot where people actually engage with your work instead of skimming past it.

If your visuals look inconsistent, low-quality, or generic, they'll assume your work is too — no matter how good your descriptions are. The solution? But what if you don't have screenshots of your work? What if you're a writer, consultant, or strategist whose deliverables aren't inherently visual?

This is where AI tools help.

Project thumbnails are the first thing people see when they land on your portfolio. They need to look professional and consistent.

The key is consistency — all your thumbnails should use the same style, size, and visual approach.

Want to show your copywriting work? Place your text on a laptop screen mockup. Need to display a strategy document? Use a clean document template with your content.

Once the groundwork is done, it's time for the moment where most people dread: building the portfolio website. But you shouldn't worry. You won't need to drag boxes around or write code. Instead, you'll use AI for it, and this is what you're about to learn in this lesson.
The Traditional Building Problem
Normally, building a portfolio website means choosing between two bad options:

1. Spend days learning a website builder, wrestling with templates that almost-but-not-quite match your vision.
  2. Hire a developer, wait weeks, pay thousands, and still need them every time you want to change something.
Both waste time and money, and you don't want it.

feedbackCorrect.text: That's right! Speed and accessibility are the real advantages. You go from idea to working site without technical skills or hiring help.

feedbackIncorrect.text: AI doesn't inherently improve SEO or exceed professional development capabilities — it removes the technical barrier so you can build without specialized knowledge.

options.label: You can build more complex features than human developers could
AI-built sites rank higher in search engines than traditional sites
You describe what you want in plain language and get a working site in minutes

blocks.text: Meet Lovable
Lovable is a prompt-to-website AI tool, and in comparison to many other site-builders, it has one great advantage.

feedbackCorrect.text: Right! Lovable works through natural language instructions, not manual layout manipulation. You describe, it builds.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Pricing and content creation vary across tools. The core difference is the interface — prompts versus drag-and-drop.

options.label: Lovable automatically writes all your content for you
You describe what you want in text instead of manually dragging elements around
Lovable hosts your site for free, while other builders charge monthly fees

blocks.question: How do you think Lovable is different from traditional website builders?

blocks.text: In short, you can think of Lovable as a translator: You speak in your language ("I want a clean homepage with my photo on the right"), and Lovable translates it into computer code (HTML, CSS, layouts). You focus on what you want — Lovable handles the rest.
blocks.title: 💡 Prompt-to-Website

blocks.text: No drag-and-drop. No template hunting. Just clear instructions that produce real results.

Working with Lovable

feedbackCorrect.text: Colors, structure, and fonts give Lovable actionable instructions. The "why" doesn't help it build — only the "what" matters.

feedbackIncorrect.text: AI needs specifications, not reasoning. Focus on concrete details that translate directly into design decisions.

Detailed explanations of why you made each design choice

blocks.text: Building Your Homepage
Now, let's build your portfolio and start with the most important page: your homepage. This is where first impressions happen.

blocks.prompt: Describe your homepage structure to Lovable with specific details.
blocks.template: Create a portfolio for [profession]. Primary color: [color]. Include [section type] with a photo [position], and an [section name] grid below.

blocks.text: See? Just like that, you got a working homepage. You referenced your visual identity (the teal color), described your layout (photo position, grid structure), and Lovable built it.
This is your foundation — you'll refine it next.

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly! Specificity wins. Colors, positions, and section names give Lovable clear instructions without unnecessary length or jargon.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Effective prompts are precise, not long. Use concrete details (colors, positions, numbers) rather than vague descriptions or technical terms.

options.label: It used professional web design terminology
It was long and detailed, giving Lovable as much information as possible
It included specific details like colors, layout positions, and exact section names

blocks.question: Looking at this result, what do you think made the prompt effective?

blocks.text:
All in all, your homepage needs:
  • Hero section — your name, headline, and photo
  • About preview — brief introduction
  • Project showcase — thumbnails of your 3-5 case studies
  • Contact CTA — clear way to reach you
This structure works for almost every professional portfolio.
blocks.title: 💡 Homepage Essentials

blocks.text: Refining With Select & Edit

Your homepage structure looks good, but let's assume you feel the text is too long. Or the spacing feels cramped. Or you want the hero section taller.

For this kind of situation, you can just describe the adjustment that you want to see, and Lovable updates just that part.

blocks.prompt: Complete the prompt to see how you can describe the change you want and see the result.
blocks.template: Make [element] [adjustment] and increase [spacing type] to [amount].

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly! Targeted edits save time and avoid accidentally breaking parts that already work. Change only what needs changing.

feedbackIncorrect.text: You can regenerate anytime, and quality isn't affected by the method. Targeted editing is simply more efficient for small adjustments.

options.label: Lovable doesn't allow you to regenerate pages once they're created
It produces higher quality results than full prompts
It's faster and preserves everything that's already working correctly

blocks.question: Why edit selectively for small changes instead of rewriting your entire prompt?

blocks.text: Adding Your Content & Assets

Your structure is solid. 

Now, it's time to populate it with the content and visuals you prepared in earlier lessons.

Upload your project thumbnails. Add your headshot to the hero section. Insert your Claude-written project descriptions.

Lovable handles the technical placement — you just provide the content and tell it where things should go.

Last note before moving on — you should work section by section: get the hero right, then the about preview, then the project grid. 

This iterative approach produces cleaner results than trying to do everything at once.
You've Built Your Homepage!

You just learned how to use AI to build a working portfolio homepage from scratch — no coding, no drag-and-drop, just clear instructions.

Your site structure is live, populated with your content, and ready to expand.
In the next lesson, you'll learn how to create dedicated case study pages — building detailed project layouts that give your work the space it needs to demonstrate your full expertise. Keep it going!

  • Prompt for targeted changes without rebuilding everything.
  • Result: a working homepage with your content and visual identity.

blocks.text: Telling Clients About Yourself

One thing you must not forget: clients don't just hire skills — they hire people. This means your "About" section is where strangers decide if they want to work with you — let's make sure it converts!

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly! People hire people they connect with. Your "About" section builds that connection by showing who you are, not just what you've done.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Credentials matter, but connection matters more. An "About" section isn't a résumé — it's a conversation starter that builds trust and rapport.

blocks.question: First, why do you think the "About" section is critical for converting visitors into clients?

blocks.text: Why About Sections Matter

In other words, people want to know: Who are you? What drives you? Why should they trust you with their project? A strong "About" section answers these questions warmly and authentically — without sounding like a corporate bio.

In this sense, you should think of your "About" section as the moment someone asks, "So, what do you do?" at a networking event.

You wouldn't recite your résumé. You'd tell your story in a way that's interesting, authentic, and makes people want to keep talking.
What Makes a Strong "About" Section
Good "About" sections usually follow a specific pattern that works across industries and experience levels.

feedbackCorrect.text: Background and motivation — these two elements create a connection and credibility without overwhelming readers with exhaustive details.

feedbackIncorrect.text: "About" sections should be focused narratives that connect on a human level, not comprehensive career documentation.

options.label: How you help clients or what value you bring
Detailed explanations of your education and certifications
What drives your work or what you care about professionally
Your professional background and what you specialize in

blocks.question: Which elements do you think this pattern includes?

blocks.text:
Now that you know what makes a strong "About" section, you can start writing yours.

This is where Claude comes in to help turn your raw information into polished, authentic copy.

blocks.exampleResponse:
Here's your "About" section:
"I'm an HR specialist with 15 years of experience helping companies build teams that actually work together. Throughout my career, I've been deeply involved in solving the human side of business — the part that doesn't show up in org charts but fundamentally determines whether teams thrive or struggle in their daily operations.
What truly drives my work? It's watching people find roles where they not only perform well but genuinely excel, and watching companies discover incredible talent they almost overlooked in their hiring processes. Over the years, I've developed a keen eye for identifying potential that others miss, and I take pride in helping organizations see what's possible when they invest in the right people.
I specialize in helping mid-sized companies refine their hiring processes from start to finish, develop comprehensive onboarding systems that actually work, and build cultures where people don't just show up — they want to stay and contribute meaningfully. My approach combines data-driven insights with genuine human understanding, because at the end of the day, business is about people.
If you're hiring for critical roles or trying to improve how your team works together, I'd love to have a conversation about how I can help you achieve your goals."

blocks.text: Making It Perfect for Everyone

Your portfolio looks great on your laptop. But over half of people will view it on their phones. If your site breaks on mobile, you're losing potential clients before they even see your work. So, in this lesson, you'll learn how to ensure your portfolio works flawlessly everywhere — and how to launch it live.
The Mobile Problem

When building a website, you usually start with its desktop version.

But since many people use phones as their primary device, there are certain factors to consider for this type of portfolio viewer.

feedbackCorrect.text: Typography, layout, and perception all matter. Broken mobile layouts make your portfolio look unfinished and suggest you don't pay attention to details.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Mobile users are actually more critical of design issues because they're harder to overlook on small screens. A broken mobile site undermines trust instantly.

options.label: Layout elements like buttons and images overlap or break on mobile
Text sizing becomes unreadable — too large or too small on smaller screens
Mobile users spend less time on sites, so design matters less
Poor mobile experience signals carelessness and unprofessionalism

blocks.question: Why does mobile optimization matter so much for portfolio sites?

blocks.text:
So, you should think of mobile optimization as quality assurance. 

You've built something good — now you need to make sure it actually works for everyone who sees it.
Checking Your Mobile View

Lovable includes a mobile preview feature that shows you exactly how your site looks on phones.

This is where you can spot problems before your viewers will: headlines that are too large, images that don't fit, buttons that overlap, and spacing that feels wrong.

See? Doesn't seem that good.

However, here is the good news: every issue you find can be fixed with a simple prompt — just like you built the original layout!
Fixing Mobile Issues
Let's say you open mobile preview and notice your hero section headline is way too large — it's breaking across multiple lines and dominating the screen.

blocks.template: For mobile, reduce all [element], photo and [navigation element], and [alignment] the text. Also, [command] contact buttons.

blocks.text:
See how that works? You identified a mobile-specific problem and fixed it without affecting the desktop layout.

This is responsive design — making sure your site adapts properly to different screen sizes.

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly! Surgical fixes save time and prevent accidental damage to working components. Change only what needs changing.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Performance isn't affected by fix method, and rebuilds are always allowed. Targeted fixes are simply more efficient and less risky.

Individual fixes load faster on mobile devices

blocks.text: Cool, right? With Lovable, publishing is effortless: no servers, no hosting setup — just click Publish in the top right corner, confirm, and wait about a minute. That's it — your portfolio goes live!

Once you publish, Lovable deploys your portfolio to a live server, generates a unique URL, and makes your site accessible to anyone with the link.

Your published site includes all functionality, styling, and content — it's fully functional, not just a preview!
Your Published Link

After publishing, you get a permanent, shareable link like yourname.lovable.app. Anyone can visit this URL without needing a Lovable account — perfect for sharing with potential clients, colleagues, or on your LinkedIn profile.

blocks.text: Published portfolios aren't frozen. You can continue editing your project normally. When you're ready, press Update in the publish dropdown, and your changes will go live. This way, you can refine your portfolio without worrying about breaking your live site mid-edit!
Connecting a Custom Domain (Optional)
Right now, your portfolio lives at yourname.lovable.app — which works perfectly fine for sharing and job applications.
But if you want a more professional custom domain like yourname.com, you can connect one.
To connect a custom domain, you'll need:

• A paid Lovable plan
  • A domain name purchased from registrars like Namecheap or GoDaddy (around $10-15/year)
Lovable handles the technical setup through a service called Entri, which configures everything automatically.
Once this part of the job is finished, your portfolio website is all set!

Before we conclude, there is one thing that most people get wrong: they think portfolios are "finished" projects you build once and forget. The truth? Portfolios are living documents that evolve with your career.

feedbackCorrect.text: Right! Regular but not obsessive updates keep your portfolio fresh without becoming a burden. Quality additions every few months show growth.

  • Click Update to push changes live.

blocks.text: Making It Perfect for Everyone

Your portfolio looks great on your laptop. But over half of people will view it on their phones. If your site breaks on mobile, you're losing potential clients before they even see your work. So, in this lesson, you'll learn how to ensure your portfolio works flawlessly everywhere — and how to launch it live.
The Mobile Problem

When building a website, you usually start with its desktop version.

But since many people use phones as their primary device, there are certain factors to consider for this type of portfolio viewer.

feedbackCorrect.text: Typography, layout, and perception all matter. Broken mobile layouts make your portfolio look unfinished and suggest you don't pay attention to details.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Mobile users are actually more critical of design issues because they're harder to overlook on small screens. A broken mobile site undermines trust instantly.

blocks.question: Why does mobile optimization matter so much for portfolio sites?

blocks.text:
So, you should think of mobile optimization as quality assurance. 

You've built something good — now you need to make sure it actually works for everyone who sees it.
Checking Your Mobile View

Lovable includes a mobile preview feature that shows you exactly how your site looks on phones.

This is where you can spot problems before your viewers will: headlines that are too large, images that don't fit, buttons that overlap, and spacing that feels wrong.

See? Doesn't seem that good.

However, here is the good news: every issue you find can be fixed with a simple prompt — just like you built the original layout!
Fixing Mobile Issues
Let's say you open mobile preview and notice your hero section headline is way too large — it's breaking across multiple lines and dominating the screen.

blocks.prompt: Fix a mobile layout issue by targeting the specific element and screen size.
blocks.template: For mobile, reduce all [element], photo and [navigation element], and [alignment] the text. Also, [command] contact buttons.

blocks.text:
See how that works? You identified a mobile-specific problem and fixed it without affecting the desktop layout.

This is responsive design — making sure your site adapts properly to different screen sizes.

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly! Surgical fixes save time and prevent accidental damage to working components. Change only what needs changing.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Performance isn't affected by fix method, and rebuilds are always allowed. Targeted fixes are simply more efficient and less risky.

options.label: You preserve everything that's already working while targeting only the problems
Lovable doesn't allow full page rebuilds once mobile issues appear
Individual fixes load faster on mobile devices

blocks.question: We've fixed one mobile issue individually rather than rebuilding the entire page. What do you think is the advantage of this approach?

feedbackCorrect.text: Typography, images, and button sizing are the most common mobile problems. Fix these, and your site will work smoothly on phones.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Color perception varies by device, but isn't typically a layout issue. Focus on sizing, spacing, and element positioning — those break mobile experiences.

options.label: Buttons that are too small to tap easily or overlap each other

Colors that look different on phone screens versus desktop monitors
